newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil soy exports could hit new high in 97-Safras.
newsitem.headline: Brazil soy exports could hit new high in 97-Safras.

text.p: Brazilian soy exports could hit a new record in 1997 with low world stocks, high prices and good weather producing a repeat of strong 1996 sales, independent consultants Safras e Mercado said.
Brazil was expected to export 17.23 million tonnes of soybeans and soy products in the 1997/98 marketing year (February to January), up six percent on the previous year.
"(This would be) the second highest volume on record with very real prospects for hitting a new record," Safras said in a weekly report.

Of this total, soybeans would account for 5.8 million tonnes, soymeal for 10.15 million and soyoil for 1.28 million -- exports of the latter two were seen falling due to the abolition of the ICMS export tax which has reduced margins for crushing.
Setting a new record would depend on a larger crop than the 26.3 million tonnes which Safras currently expects.
An upward revision of this forecast is possible due to the good weather which has prevailed since the end of January in the main soybean growing regions, it said.
Export premiums were set to remain 20 to 30 percent above average as world stocks fell to their lowest levels since 1983/84.
Brazil earned a record $4.46 million from sales of soybeans and soyproducts in 1996, up 17 percent from the previous year, according to Commerce Department figures published by Safras.
But total volume, at 16.20 million tonnes, was eight percent below the record volume set in 1994.
The European Union accounted for 82 percent of soybean exports and 70 percent of soymeal exports. Sales grew in non-traditional markets, with Poland buying five percent of soymeal exports.
China remained the main destination for soyoil, accounting for 59 percent of total sales.
Safras estimates Brazil will have imported 1.3 million tonnes of soybeans, 150,000 tonnes of soymeal and 200,000 of crude soyoil during the 1996/97 marketing year.
